You're both overlooking the concept of inertia.

If you're driving down the highway and drop a tennis ball out the window the moment you pass a flag pole, the tennis ball won't bounce up and down beside the flag poll; it will continue to bounce down the highway in the direction the car was going because it has inertia (though from the car's perspective it will fall behind the car because it is no longer accelerating, but it decelerating due to air resistance and friction form bouncing, but its net movement is still in the same direction of the car, relative to ground).

If you jump up in the air, the Earth does not move out from under your feet; you don't land in a different spot than you jumped from, because you share your inertia with the Earth.

If a helicopter hovers in one spot, the ground beneath it will stay the same because it maintains the same inertia as the Earth. If a plane could someone freeze in place, the same would be true; the Earth wouldn't move out from under it because it would still share the inertia of the Earth (weird things would happen due to air resistance, but in general its position would stay the same).
